application_guidance.input_pattern: Stored productive and nonproductive cuts plus nonnegative weights normalized over productive steps.
read_original_when: Using inexact Oracle responses or approximate linear minimization.
Changing normalization, feasibility model or output metric.
sensitive_conditions: Separation sign and validity on int X; extension to X uses solidity.
Normalization is over I only; nonproductive weights may be positive.
Residual includes all steps, output average includes productive steps only.
Mathematical validity needs a containing solid; exact computation additionally needs linear optimization over B.

content.intended_use: A posteriori objective-gap certification; not an unrestricted Oracle Complexity bound.

proofs.full_local_argument: Complete source-faithful exposition of the short argument, not a new local Theorem: For t∈I and x∈X, F(x)≥F(x^t)+<e_t,x−x^t>. For t∈J, the strict separator inequality on int X extends by continuity of the linear form to <e_t,x−x^t>≤0 on X, since X is the closure of int X. Multiplying by ξ_t≥0, summing, and using Σ_Iξ_t=1 gives F(x)≥A+Σ_tξ_t<e_t,x−x^t>≥A−r. Therefore Opt≥F_*; subtraction proves (i), including extended-real objective values at boundary points. For (ii), the finite productive set is nonempty, so a best point exists and lies in int X. The weights on I form a convex combination, so xbar∈int X. Convexity gives F(xbar)≤A, and minimality gives F(xbest)≤A. Together with Opt≥A−r, these prove both residual bounds. The closure explanation makes explicit the elementary extension used in the source's Introduction argument; it is not an additional scientific dependency or transfer claim.
proofs.locator: Introduction, PDF page 3 top / printed page 2; §6.1, PDF page 22 / printed page 21, equation (46)
map: Source argument for (i): subgradient inequalities at productive queries and separation inequalities at nonproductive queries are multiplied by their respective nonnegative weights and summed.
For every x∈X, F(x)≥A−Σ_t ξ_t<e_t,x^t−x>≥A−r=F_*. Minimizing over X yields F_*≤Opt and then equation (9).

Source argument for (ii): xbest is an interior query and xbar is a convex combination of interior queries. Convexity and normalization give A≥F(xbar), while A≥F(xbest). Thus F_*≥F(xbar)−r and F_*≥F(xbest)−r; combine with (i).

assumptions: X⊂R^n is compact convex with nonempty interior.
F:X→R∪{+∞} is closed convex and finite on int X.
B⊃X is a solid: compact convex with nonempty interior.
The protocol uses the Separation and First order Oracle responses specified above; I is nonempty.
Every ξ_t is nonnegative and Σ_{t∈I}ξ_t=1. Weights over J need not sum to zero or form part of this normalization.
statement.conclusion: (i) F_*≤Opt. Consequently ε_opt(xhat)≤F(xhat)−F_* for every feasible xhat∈X. (ii) xbest and xbar both belong to int X, and F(xbest)−Opt≤r and F(xbar)−Opt≤r.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Work in R^n with the usual pairing. Let Opt=min_{x∈X}F(x). A τ-step protocol consists of x^t,e_t for t=1,...,τ, I={t:x^t∈int X} and J={1,...,τ}\I. For t∈I, e_t∈∂F(x^t); for t∈J, <e_t,y><<e_t,x^t> for all y∈int X. Given ξ, define r=max_{x∈B}Σ_{t=1}^τ ξ_t<e_t,x^t−x>, A=Σ_{t∈I}ξ_tF(x^t), F_*=A−r, xbar=Σ_{t∈I}ξ_tx^t, and xbest=x^s for any s∈argmin_{t∈I}F(x^t). Define ε_opt(x)=F(x)−Opt.
statement.parameter_domains: n is a positive integer; τ is a positive integer; x^t,e_t∈R^n and ξ∈R_+^τ. Compact B and finitely many finite vectors make r finite. No smoothness, Lipschitz constant or strong convexity is assumed.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such CMP, every finite associated productive protocol, every such containing solid B and every certificate ξ, conclusions (i)–(ii) hold. The bound is deterministic for the realized protocol and certificate; (i) applies to every feasible xhat∈X.
